question: A donor deposits ₹8,00,000 in a trust that earns 10% simple interest annually. The interest is used to distribute three annual awards. If the second and third awards are ₹35,000 and ₹20,000 respectively, what is the value of the first award?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total annual interest earned = 10% of 8,00,000 = ₹80,000.

Combined value of the 2nd and 3rd awards = 35,000 + 20,000 = ₹55,000.

Value of the 1st award = Total interest − Combined value of other two awards.

Value of the 1st award = 80,000 − 55,000 = ₹25,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal deposit (P) = ₹8,00,000

Rate of interest (R) = 10% per annum

Time (T) = 1 year (for annual awards distribution)

Value of the second award = ₹35,000

Value of the third award = ₹20,000

 
 
 Principal: ₹8,00,000
 
 
 
• 
 

 10% SI

 
 
 Interest: ₹80,000

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 

 
 
 1st Award: ?
 
 
 2nd Award: ₹35,000

 
 3rd Award: ₹20,000

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total Interest = (8,00,000 × 10 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ Total Interest = 80,000

Since the total interest generated covers exactly the three awards:

⇒ Total Interest = 1st Award + 2nd Award + 3rd Award

⇒ 80,000 = 1st Award + 35,000 + 20,000

⇒ 80,000 = 1st Award + 55,000

⇒ 1st Award = 80,000 − 55,000

⇒ 1st Award = 25,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Endowment Funds and Perpetuity

When a principal amount is deposited in a trust to distribute regular annual awards without touching the initial deposit, it behaves like a perpetuity. The annual payout generated is exactly equal to the annual interest earned (Payout = P × R).

Simple Interest Direct Formula

Simple Interest is calculated uniformly on the base principal amount. Total Interest after t years = P × R × t ÷ 100. If evaluated annually, t = 1, leading to directly finding the given percentage of the principal.

Interest vs Amount

Interest is the extra earning on the deposit, while Amount is the total sum returned. Amount = P + I = P[1 + (RT ÷ 100)]. In trust or charity fund questions, the awards are strictly tied only to the Interest portion, preserving the original Principal Amount.
